text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Streaming SLO breached in eu-west (p99 > 5s) for /v1/stream. Detected chunk-gap pattern and repeated client disconnects. Incident INC-2026-033 created.

dave_oncall: taking this. Starting triage — p95 ~2200ms, p99 ~6800ms. Spike began ~12:14 UTC. Affects SSE + websocket paths.

alice: noted. Any recent deploys or config changes in the eu streaming proxy? Can someone check proxy timeouts/keepalives and upstream write errors?

ben: checking proxy logs now. Seeing a lot of `write timeout` and `client slowconsumer` on proxy nodes eu-proxy-{01..04}. Grep: `kubectl logs -n streaming eu-proxy | grep "write timeout"` shows repeated hits starting 12:13.

carmen: Support: two customers reported truncated responses and one 504 from our streaming endpoint. Ticket #SR-8142 linked. Might be client-side backpressure + proxy enforcement.

support-bot: Customer impact: partial for 2 orgs (~0.4% of streaming requests in EU) — retries causing visible user issues in production apps.

deploy-bot: Last config rollout to eu-proxy completed 11:50 UTC (no canary failures). No code deploys to runtime since 10:00 UTC.

ben: quick metric dump: upstream write queue size spiked, socket send error rate +5x. Kernel-level tx buffer full seen on some nodes. Also seeing increased long tail on KV cache evictions at same time.

dave_oncall: ok, hypothesis: proxy keepalive / write-timeout settings too aggressive for a subset of slow consumer clients. Mitigation options: 1) bump proxy write timeout from 15s -> 30s, 2) scale proxy replicas, 3) enable temporary per-tenant fallback to polling endpoints for affected customers. Which first?

alice: prefer minimal blast radius — try 1) bump timeout + scale by 2 replicas. Prepare k8s patch and monitor. If we still see p99 > 5s after 5m, do 3).

ben: applying patch to eu-proxy config now (rolling restart). Command: `kubectl -n streaming set env ds/eu-proxy PROXY_WRITE_TIMEOUT=30s` then `kubectl rollout restart ds/eu-proxy` — doing this in canary across 1 node first.

(2m later)

ben: canary eu-proxy-01 updated, observing reduced `write timeout` logs on that node. p99 dropped to ~3.2s for canary subset.

dave_oncall: scale started +2 replicas. Routing change pushed to avoid overloaded AZ. Also temporarily flagged the two affected tenants to route to non-streaming fallback — support notified.

carmen: customer rollback request: one customer asked to rollback middleware change on their side, but they confirmed waiting for our mitigation.

ben: after full rollout of timeout bump + scale, global p99 improved to ~1.05s, p95 ~650ms. No new truncated responses reported in the last 4m.

dave_oncall: confirming: incident impact largely mitigated. Actions: 1) keep patched timeout for 24h, 2) run postmortem to understand why write buffers filled (client slowconsumers vs kernel backlog vs proxy scheduling), 3) add anomaly alert for sudden KV eviction + socket tx backlog correlation. I'll hand this to oncall for post-incident follow-up.

alice: +1. Please capture exact node ids and sample tcpdump from before/after for forensic. Ben, save logs and open a trace link.

ben: logs archived to s3://redwood-logs/incidents/INC-2026-033.tar.gz. Trace link: https://traces.internal/re/INC-2026-033

dave_oncall: closing incident channel for live mitigation. Will schedule a brief incident debrief in 1 business day. Thanks all :thumbsup:

carmen: noted, I'll coordinate customer comms update and follow-up with support.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: INC-2026-033 — p99 returned to normal range. Follow-up: postmortem required.

alice: thanks team. Please add suggested runbook tweak for `PROXY_WRITE_TIMEOUT` and an automated canary check for slowconsumer patterns.

dave_oncall: acknowledged. End of thread.
